target_customer: Defense, commercial and medical supply customers needing long-range cargo delivery
problem: Time-critical cargo over long distances is slow and costly by road or crewed aircraft, and small delivery drones lacked range and payload.
business_model: Hardware sales and drone delivery service contracts

founders.name: Hannan Parvizian
founders.background_notes: Tesla role from Wikipedia snippet; education not found.

founders.name: Wesley Zheng
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in the company description on the YC listing.

exit.reason: Asset purchase after an assignment for the benefit of creditors filed in August 2022; deal closed Sept 30, 2022.

competitors.name: Zipline
competitors.what: Short-range medical delivery drones, fixed wing

competitors.name: Matternet
competitors.what: Quadcopter delivery network for medical and urban cargo

technical_complexity.rationale: Designing and flying long-range, high-payload autonomous VTOL aircraft required aerospace engineering and regulatory work well beyond a small software team.

defensibility.rationale: Aircraft design and contracts were hard to copy, but many VTOL cargo entrants appeared and no unique data or network effect existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: In 2022 Sierra Nevada Corporation bought the Voly assets and about 30 employees after venture funding dried up.

market_need_then: In 2017 TechCrunch covered a 100-mile demonstration in Austin, showing interest in long-range B2B express delivery; medical and defense logistics were the stated targets.

branding.domain_note: Company site later at flyvoly.com under the Voly product name; Wikipedia says it was formerly styled Volans-i.
branding.brand_signature: VOLY product line names (Voly M20, Voly 50)

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press coverage existed but no sources show a strong consumer-facing or community brand; name meaning not sourced.

outcome_analysis: Volansi raised about $75M across a Series A and a $50M Series B in September 2020, then reportedly lost $75M in promised financing; it filed an assignment for the benefit of creditors in August 2022 and Sierra Nevada bought its assets for an undisclosed price on Sept 30, 2022. Capital-intensive aerospace hardware, a tightening funding market and lost commitments left it unable to finance the next stage.
notes: The Series A date and amount come from a search summary of Series B coverage and were not seen in a primary release; one source called the Series B a Series C. The company website flyvoly.com returned no readable content. Competitor entries are from a 2016 article; their funding was not captured. Seed funding before the Series A was not found. Status is Acquired in YC but the deal was a distressed asset purchase.
